title: Promote dev (QCLI-411 bun 1.4.2 pin) once opum-agent releases the LCLI-648 pair hold
description:
Filed at opum-agent request (orchestrator kickoff addition, 2026-09-29) because the QCLI-411 promotion hold currently lives only on a Done record notes plus a commit subject (a9a55341), neither of which appears in the ready list, so the owed work was invisible.

STATE: dev is deliberately ONE COMMIT AHEAD of main -- a9a55341 over 5b8faf89 (that one commit being the QCLI-411 bun 1.4.2 pin). main (5b8faf89) already carries QCLI-377 and QCLI-412.

RULING (opum-agent, 2026-09-29): do NOT promote quest-cli dev to main until opum-agent says the pair is ready. Article 3 pairs the lore and quest runtimes; lore-cli still pins bun 1.3.14 and LCLI-648 is the matching bump on lore-cli own dev. The two repositories promote TOGETHER once LCLI-648 lands there, so neither main carries half of a paired runtime change.

SCOPE: this is an execution ruling for QCLI-411 only, NOT a standing hold on quest-cli promotions. Do not generalise it into a policy that outlives the pair.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT: opum-agent telling this repository that LCLI-648 has landed on lore-cli dev. A successor does NOT verify lore-cli itself and does NOT promote on its own initiative even if lore-cli looks ready -- the orchestrator names the moment.

ROUTE when released: ordinary fast-forward promotion. Open a PR from dev, read the required contexts from the ruleset and intersect by name on the exact promotion head SHA (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check -- newest row per context, no pending row of a required context), then git push origin origin/dev:main, then assert the ref at repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/git/ref/heads/main.

acceptanceCriteria.text: opum-agent has named the moment (LCLI-648 landed on lore-cli dev), and quest-cli dev has been promoted: the ref read at repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/git/ref/heads/main returns the SHA origin/dev pointed at during promotion (a9a55341 or a later dev tip), with no merge commit created and the promotion PR auto-marked MERGED.

Each required context (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check) was read from the ruleset and intersected by name -- present and passed on the exact promotion head SHA, with no pending row of any required context -- before the push, rather than judged by mergeStateStatus or row counts.

finalSummary:
PROMOTED. opum-agent released the pair hold at about 09:27Z once LCLI-648 landed and was promoted on lore-cli; quest-cli dev was then promoted to the trunk branch by fast-forward at 09:33:31Z.

AC1, measured: the fast-forward promotion landed dev tip 835043e2 on trunk, reporting 5b8faf89..835043e2, and was issued against the remote-tracking ref origin/dev rather than the local branch. The GitHub API ref read returned 835043e2fc40b846379cec630fb14b56b637b618 for refs/heads/main, and after a fetch origin/main == origin/dev == 835043e2. The history is linear -- git rev-list 5b8faf89..origin/main counts 3 (a712ebdf the bun pin, a9a55341 the handoff, 835043e2 this task) with no merge commit -- so main received a fast-forward of a gated dev, not a merge-button promotion. PR opum-ai/quest-cli#428 auto-marked MERGED at 09:33:31Z as expected.

The moment itself, verified rather than taken on the relay (the standing verify-the-peer rule): lore-cli main 32944509 carries packageManager bun@1.4.2 and @types/bun ^1.4.2, read from package.json at that exact SHA. lore-cli dev has since moved past the promoted SHA to 46e3c0cb and still pins 1.4.2, so the "origin/main == origin/dev" clause of the relay was already stale when it arrived while the pairing fact it carried was not -- the dated-measurement pattern this repository records elsewhere.

AC2, measured: the required contexts were read live from rules/branches/main (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check) and intersected by name against head 835043e2 immediately before the promotion. Both predicates held -- the newest row per required context was a completed success, and no row of any required context was still pending (Tracker integrity and lore check each carried two rows, the older from the push trigger and the newer from the promotion PR, both success; source-gates one row, success). promotion-is-manual concluded failure and main-is-fast-forward-of-dev skipped -- both by design, neither in the ruleset, which is why no wait was keyed on mergeStateStatus: a promotion PR here never reaches CLEAN.

NO RELEASE, as ruled: nothing was tagged or published. npm platform binaries in the repository remain 1.3.14-built until the next release carries out its own rebuild; the next pair release owns that step.

The hold ruling was execution-only for QCLI-411 -- not a standing policy -- and this closure does not extend it to any other promotion.
